domain_title: Architecture, security, robustness, safety and evaluation
title: Implicit-trust AI architecture
canonical_definition: The system relies on prompts, conventions or developer intent instead of enforceable architectural controls.

conditions: All AI systems; isolation depth is risk- and stage-dependent.
Record the assessed release, operating scope and evidence that supports any applicability decision.

primary_questions.question: Does the case exhibit Implicit-trust AI architecture: The system relies on prompts, conventions or developer intent instead of enforceable architectural controls.
Do implemented workflows, data paths or operations show shared credentials across environments, prompts used as security boundaries, or prototypes reaching production resources?
Does current evidence test presence or scoped absence of Implicit-trust AI architecture, or does it remain unknown?

antipattern_indicators: System prompt used as security boundary

conditions: Refer verified implicit-trust ai architecture to the accountable authority before progression where the condition materially affects the requested operating scope.

normative_source_mappings.relevant_locator: NIST AI 100-1, MAP 4.2 (PDF p. 32), MEASURE 2.7 (PDF p. 35)
normative_source_mappings.mapping_rationale: The voluntary framework provides guidance on mapping internal component controls and evaluating security and resilience. The SAE criteria define the object-specific rules. Confirm any binding obligation through the accountable authority and its applicable source.

failure_mechanism: The declared or implemented control can be unreliable where security boundaries are described as prompt behavior or developer convention with no enforcement point. The mechanism can have an operational effect where verified configuration or scoped testing shows a shared credential or a request reaching an unauthorized tenant or environment.
potential_consequences: A system path can reach resources outside the intended trust boundary.

atomic_tests.test: Compare the effective governance and design records. Determine whether security boundaries are described as prompt behavior or developer convention with no enforcement point. Identify the system scope and the record that supports each conclusion.

Trace actual configurations or activity for the assessed release. Determine whether verified configuration or scoped testing shows a shared credential or a request reaching an unauthorized tenant or environment. Attribute each observation to the specific path, time and decision.

Independently review versioned review of identity, network, secret and tenant controls with controlled denied requests and recorded results. Record whether each material mechanism was tested, the observed result and the scope limitations.

required_evidence.title: Effective design and governance records
required_evidence.description: Review the versioned owner decision and relevant specifications for evidence of whether security boundaries are described as prompt behavior or developer convention with no enforcement point. Preserve material conflict and applicability context.

required_evidence.title: Observed condition or enforcement trace
required_evidence.description: Use effective configuration or dated operational records to determine whether verified configuration or scoped testing shows a shared credential or a request reaching an unauthorized tenant or environment. Identify the version, affected paths and period represented.

required_evidence.title: Executed scoped comparison
required_evidence.description: Provide versioned review of identity, network, secret and tenant controls with controlled denied requests and recorded results. Include current scope, expected results, observed results, retained evidence and unresolved cases.

required_evidence.title: Independent review and limitations
required_evidence.description: An independent reviewer confirms the assessed version, completeness of coverage, result, limitations and whether a material change requires a new test.

required_artifacts: Versioned review of identity, network, secret and tenant controls with controlled denied requests and recorded results.
Current version and scope with all material failure paths and cases identified.
Expected and observed results, attributable records, and independent review of coverage and residual limitations.

sufficiency: Presence requires affirmative evidence for a material mechanism. Examine whether security boundaries are described as prompt behavior or developer convention with no enforcement point, and separately check whether verified configuration or scoped testing shows a shared credential or a request reaching an unauthorized tenant or environment. A supported mechanism may establish presence within its evidenced scope.
Keep unresolved or contradictory mechanisms UNKNOWN and preserve the competing records. Refer material interpretation conflicts to the accountable human authority.

Use TESTED_ABSENT only after a current, executed, successful and independently verified evaluation covers all material paths within scope. Use versioned review of identity, network, secret and tenant controls with controlled denied requests and recorded results. Reassess when material changes affect that scope.
evidence_rules.evidence_ceiling: A document can identify a declared gap. Effective configuration can demonstrate a reachable condition. Observed records support only their covered period and workflow. TESTED_ABSENT requires the complete scoped absence contract.
false_positive_guards: A shared underlying service can be permitted when independently enforced tenant and resource isolation is evidenced.
Confirm that the observed or alleged condition applies to the current assessed release and a reachable path.
prohibited_inferences: A gap or UNKNOWN in D1 alone cannot establish AP-D1 presence.
Missing complaints, incident silence and unsuccessful collection cannot establish absence.
Model output and tactic selection grant no authority to approve, close a finding or accept risk.

finding_definitions.title: Design or intent shows implicit-trust ai architecture
Implementation or operating evidence shows implicit-trust ai architecture
Presence or tested absence of implicit-trust ai architecture is unresolved within scope
